articles.headline: Yankees' Aaron Judge returning to injured list with calf strain
articles.description: Yankees slugger Aaron Judge is returning to the IL after suffering a right calf strain. He had played just seven games since returning from a lengthy absence for a broken rib.
articles.body:
Three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge will miss most or all of the rest of the regular season after the New York Yankees announced Friday they are placing him on the 10-day injured list because of a right calf strain.

New York said it will make the roster move Saturday. The placement could be backdated to Thursday, meaning it is possible Judge could return for New York's regular-season finale on Sept. 27.

Judge was pulled from Wednesday's loss to the Twins because of tightness in his lower right leg. An inning earlier, he had to run to the gap to track down a ball in the outfield, but he didn't show any sign of discomfort or slowness and later said he first felt tightness during the first inning.

Judge was 4 for 26 with 13 strikeouts and one extra-base hit in seven games since returning last week from a broken rib, which kept him out of the lineup for more than three months.

The Yankees, who have clinched at least a wild-card spot, trail the first-place Tampa Bay Rays by five games in the American League East entering Friday.

Judge is hitting .241 with 18 home runs and 41 RBIs in 66 games this season.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: USMNT's Balogun makes season debut for Monaco after failed transfer
articles.description: United States striker Folarin Balogun made his first appearance of the season for AS Monaco in its 2-1 win over Lens on Friday.
articles.body:
United States striker Folarin Balogun made his first appearance of the season for AS Monaco in its 2-1 win over Lens on Friday.

It was Balogun's first outing since a proposed transfer to Premier League side Everton dramatically broke down in the final hours of the transfer window at the start of this month.

- USMNT's post-World Cup squad is missing stars

- Poch: Balogun must find 'best place to perform

- Belgium won't back Infantino bid, cite Balogun decision

The 25-year-old came off the substitutes' bench in the 76th minute as Monaco remained unbeaten at the top of Ligue 1.

Just a couple of weeks ago, Balogun's future appeared elsewhere. Terms had been agreed between Monaco and Everton, as well as with the player, but questions raised by Everton about his medical saw Balogun pull the plug on the deal.

Despite Monaco subsequently saying that it would continue to explore a possible move for Balogun to a league where the transfer window remained open, he now looks set to stay put, at least until the transfer window reopens across much of Europe in January.

Balogun, who had also been battling a minor injury, had not played a competitive game since his controversial end to the 2026 World Cup.

The former Arsenal forward took the field in the U.S. men's national team's round-of-16 loss to Belgium after a one-game suspension for a red card in the previous game was surprisingly overturned by FIFA, with U.S. President Donald Trump acknowledging that he made a personal appeal to FIFA chief Gianni Infantino.

Balogun, who scored three goals at the World Cup, was not named this week in coach Mauricio Pochettino's first USMNT roster since the tournament.

Monaco, meanwhile, has continued its impressive start to the season under new coach Filipe Luis.

Paris Brunner put Monaco ahead in the 32nd minute on Friday, but Matthieu Udol equalized in the 57th. Jonathan Gradit then scored an own goal in the 84th.

Brunner is still awaiting a likely sanction for a throat-slitting gesture during a goal celebration last weekend.

Lens coach Dino Toppmöller was dismissed in the week after just six games in charge.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Texans rule WR Nico Collins out vs. Bengals with hamstring injury
articles.description: The Texans have ruled star wide receiver Nico Collins out for Sunday's matchup against the Bengals due to a hamstring injury.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Texans star wide receiver Nico Collins was ruled out for Houston's Week 2 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after suffering a hamstring injury during a mid-week practice.

Collins was healthy to start Wednesday's practice, but he tweaked his hamstring later in the session. The injury doesn't appear to be long term. Collins met with team doctors after Wednesday's practice and the injury isn't believed to be "serious," a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The Texans' official injury report listed Collins as limited in Wednesday's practice due to the injury. He was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's and Friday's practice.

Collins, 27, also battled a hamstring injury in 2024, when he was placed on injured reserve and missed five games in the middle of the season. He opened 2026 with seven receptions on 10 targets for 75 yards -- all team highs -- and a touchdown in the Texans' Week 1 loss at home to the Buffalo Bills. The six-year veteran has been Houston's leading receiver in each of the last three seasons, eclipsing 1,000 receiving yards in each campaign.

Collins' absence is another blow to the wideout room which already lost receiver Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL during joint practices with the Las Vegas Raiders last month. Higgins was projected to be the Texans' No. 2 wideout alongside Collins as the 2025 second-round pick had a strong training camp coming off a rookie campaign with 525 receiving yards and six touchdowns as a rookie.

After the loss of Higgins, Houston acquired wide receiver Kayshon Boutte in a trade with the New England Patriots in late August.

The main group of receivers going into Week 2 will be Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchison, Jared Wayne and Boutte.

The Texans also ruled starting right guard Ed Ingram out for the game with a groin injury.

articles.headline: FBI case against fake 49ers player adds more alleged victims
articles.description: The FBI has identified 35 additional women who say they were defrauded by Daejon Love and Taylor Chan, bringing the total number of alleged victims in a case that included Love impersonating as a 49ers player to more than 60.
articles.body:
The FBI has identified 35 additional women who say they were defrauded by Daejon Love and Taylor Chan, the agency said Friday, bringing the total number of alleged victims in a case that included Love impersonating as a San Francisco 49ers player to more than 60.

Portland FBI Special Agent in Charge Doug Olson said the agency is working to verify that the 35 women are victims of Love and Chan.

"We were surprised how many people were victimized in such a short period of time and then to have that many more come forward," Olson said at a news conference. "It's a large volume for just a couple of subjects. Our concern is that this fraud could be replicated by other individuals that are out there victimizing other people in similar schemes."

Olson said the FBI believes there are more victims of Love and Chan who have yet to come forward. He encouraged anyone with information on the two men to contact the Portland FBI.

"We don't want anyone to be fearful of coming forward," Olson said, "certainly not for fear of embarrassment or anything like that, because we want to help them and we want to make sure that this doesn't happen to anybody else."

The FBI opened its investigation into Love and Chan on Sept. 30, 2024, over allegations that date from February 2022 to Aug. 24, 2026, the day the two men were arrested at the Boise, Idaho, airport. They have been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud.

According to the criminal complaint, Love and Chan stole more than $1.3 million from 26 known victims in at least four states. The complaint alleges that Love, 35, used social media and dating apps to build fake identities, including posing as a 49ers player and a wealthy Swiss real estate investor, and convince women to send him money. Chan, 18, sometimes posed as his financial adviser and assisted Love in convincing the women that Love would invest their money with Chan.

"The victims in this case were targeted precisely because they were trusting, responsible people who they believed were building genuine relationships and legitimate financial futures," Olson said. "... They were deliberately manipulated through an extremely sophisticated scheme that blended fake personas, fabricated investment accounts, staged video calls and AI-reinforced false identities."

Olson said the fraud scheme was "bespoke" to each victim. Not every woman got the Niners player persona, but Olson said Love often relied on the professional athlete character to reinforce his income level.

"He was either a player, former player, a player on injured reserve, and whatever name he was using, he'd put enough stuff into the media searches so it was the first thing that came up on people's [Google] page," Olson said. "And it was not just the first thing that came up; it was like there were multiple things in there that would confirm whatever he was telling those folks.. ... articles.headline: Heat, Pelle Larsson agree to 4-year, $60M extension
articles.description: The Heat and guard Pelle Larsson have reached agreement on a four-year, $60 million extension his agents told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
Miami Heat guard Pelle Larsson has agreed to a new four-year, $60 million contract extension, with a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Austin Brown and Steven Heumann of CAA Sports told ESPN on Friday.

A second-round find in the 2024 draft, the 6-foot-5 guard avoids restricted free agency next summer and locks in a new deal with a mutual option that fully guarantees $60 million while allowing either side to opt-in on 2030.

Larsson has become a foundation piece for the Heat amid their offseason overhaul. He is set to have a major rotation role for Larsson, who averaged 11.4 points per game last season, up nearly 7 points per game from his rookie season. Larsson also ranked fourth-best in offensive efficiency in Miami, per ESPN Research, and fifth in minutes played.

Larsson started 54 of the 70 games he played last season, and ranked in the top-10 in charges drawn last season, according to ESPN Research.

Miami's biggest offseason splash was the acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo in a trade that saw a package headlined by Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. going back to Milwaukee. The Heat also signed free agent Klay Thompson after he cleared waivers following a buyout agreement with the Dallas Mavericks.

Miami looks to return to the postseason after missing the playoffs last season for the first time in seven seasons.

articles.headline: Bills to take time with Ed Oliver, DJ Moore injuries
articles.description: A long week will give more time for Bills defensive lineman Ed Oliver (hip) and wide receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) to get healthy following Thursday's injuries.
articles.body:
Call it a not-so-mad scramble.

The Buffalo Bills lost defensive lineman Ed Oliver and wide receiver DJ Moore to injury before and during their 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night. As coach Joe Brady told reporters on Friday, the team will slow-play the evaluation process with both Oliver and Moore.

The Bills don't return to the practice field until Sept. 23, and as such Brady said he's holding off on rushing judgments or prognoses on the two starters until the team can see what rest does for them.

Moore is considered day-to-day with a shoulder injury sustained in the second quarter of the win over Detroit that's not considered serious, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Oliver, meanwhile, didn't play against Detroit. He sustained the hip injury just minutes before the pregame deadline for players to be ruled inactive. Brady said Friday that Oliver was in the training room getting evaluated about three minutes before the deadline came, which forced the Bills to make a quickfire choice about one of their cornerstone defensive linemen.

"If it was normal maybe you'd have an hour or so to run some tests and see what happens," Brady said. "We didn't have that time. We just had to make the decisions."

Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard described Oliver -- who's logged 30 sacks and 57 TFLs across eight seasons in Buffalo, but missed 14 games last year with injuries -- as a player you build a gameplan around. Removing his presence from the gameplan barely an hour before kickoff creates a scramble, but not one Leonhard would describe as "frantic."

Leonhard said the minutes following Oliver's deactivation consisted of meetings with defensive position coaches to strategize not just who'd replace Oliver in certain packages, but also conversations about what the domino effect in the rotations would be and which packages needed to be eliminated entirely.

"It's not necessarily just one chess piece away," Leonhard said. "It's a couple moves away that we'd have some deviations. Just trying to go through all the scenarios of what can happen and make sure all the depth and the rotations are going to be in a situation to allow you to play 45 snaps or 85 snaps. That's the uncertainty; you never know how the game is going to play out."

The Bills return to action in Week 3 with a home game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 27.

articles.headline: How can erratic Chelsea find stability? For starters: Look to Brentford
articles.description: Brentford's 3-0 thrashing of Chelsea served as a humbling reminder of what a well-run club can accomplish.
articles.body:
LONDON -- You could forgive Chelsea's new outright owners for casting an envious glance at Brentford on Friday evening.

Chelsea might have fresh clarity at the helm of the club and a much-admired manager, Xabi Alonso, in charge, but familiar issues remain. Brentford's 3-0 victory meant Chelsea's era of full Clearlake Capital control started with a humbling reminder of what a club with a settled identity looks like.

Chelsea remain in a state of flux, but it wasn't meant to be like this again. Their investment in the summer was meant to build a spine: midfielder Jordan Henderson and striker Danny Welbeck were there to bring solidity and experience. The signings were in Alonso's image. But this defeat was a carbon copy of last season's Chelsea: a limp effort from a side that teeters on the abyss of mid-match capitulation.

Chelsea's attack has been impressive this season, but without João Pedro up front, the previously deadly triumvirate of Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer missed their point person as striker Danny Welbeck was unable to click with the duo. Instead, what we saw from Chelsea was an organized performance for about 70 minutes, Henderson and Valentín Barco bringing some stability in front of the back four.

The match was even at that juncture, chances at a premium. But once the substitutions came and the legs tired, Brentford were ready to pounce. Muscle memory clicked in. They remained resolute at the back, patient in attack, completely comfortable in their own skin and with full clarity over who they are as a club both on and off the pitch.

All of Brentford's three goals will make ugly viewing for Chelsea. The hosts' first goal was from a corner -- a ball from Mikkel Damsgaard, a header back across the box from Jannik Schuster to Jaidon Anthony, who was unmarked at the far post to nod home. Their second was from a counterattack -- Chelsea were left empty at the back, Kevin Schade darted away and after his shot was well-saved, and Igor Thiago acrobatically converted the rebound home. And then came the final one, as Fábio Carvalho finished at the far post unmarked. Brentford coach Keith Andrews jumped into his assistants' arms and looked to the sky, as those in red and white chanted how they'd love to play Chelsea every week.

Brentford seems to be one of the happiest places on football's earth. They were unbeaten heading into Friday's match with a win and three draws. Frustrated sporting directors must look their way after another successful summer transfer window where much-admired midfielder Mamadou Sangare was brought over from Lens, and several other players were nurtured and improved here.

While Alonso was fielding pre-match questions on injuries and ownership changes, Andrews' pre-match news conference was more of a celebration: Schade and Vitaly Janelt had been called up by Jurgen Klopp to his 44-man Germany squad, and Nathan Collins' had made a £1,000 donation to Brentford supporters' group TW8 Casuals to help fund supporters'

articles.headline: Brentford 3-0 Chelsea: Premier League action as Bees sink Xabi Alonso's Blues - as it happened
articles.description: Goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho see Brentford beat Chelsea. Follow reaction with ESPN.
articles.body:
Brentford earned their first ever win over Chelsea in the Premier League on Friday after a 3-0 victory at the GTech.

The hosts move up to third in the table ahead of the rest of the weekend's fixtures and remain unbeaten in the Premier League this season. 

It was a puzzling display for Xabi Alonso to ponder after watching his team impose themselves on the hosts in the first half yet struggling to find a goal threat, before succumbing in the second period to goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho.

- Xabi Alonso thanks Todd Boehly, Mark Walter after Chelsea sale

- João Pedro withdraws from Brazil squad with injury

It's been another eventful week behind the scenes at Chelsea with the news that co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes in the club. 

Boehly and Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea -- having each owned 12.83% -- to give Clearlake Capital -- which previously held 61.5% -- full control of the London club.

The consortium bought Chelsea in 2022 for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion), with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment. The club's sale came after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned by alleged ties to Russia president Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, will remain a partner in the ownership group, the club has confirmed.

Chelsea manager Alonso said it was time to "move on together."

"I think it is an important day for the club when there is an important change in the structure of the club, new ownership," Alonso told a news conference on Thursday.

"Thanks to the former owners for what they have done. I was not here but I know that they played an important role. And now that Behdad [Eghbali] is taking more control, or almost full control, I think it is good that the main one is clear."

articles.headline: Ravens' Zay Flowers doubtful vs. Saints; Nnamdi Madubuike out
articles.description: Ravens receiver Zay Flowers is doubtful for Sunday's game vs. the Saints after he aggravated a left hamstring injury and missed the majority of practices this week.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- It looks like the Baltimore Ravens will be without Lamar Jackson's favorite target as receiver Zay Flowers is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

Flowers missed a majority of practices this week after aggravating a left hamstring injury in the Ravens' season-opening 41-23 win at the Indianapolis Colts.

The loss of Flowers would be significant. Over the last 18 games, he has 91 catches for 1,361 yards. During that same stretch, the Ravens' other wide receivers have combined for 55 catches for 814 yards.

If Flowers can't play, Rashod Bateman becomes the most familiar target for Jackson. The other four healthy wide receivers are LaJohntay Wester, Devontez Walker, Elijah Sarratt and Chris Moore.

"The confidence that I have in the guys is really high," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "It comes from the amount of reps that everybody has gotten all the way back to OTAs, all the way through training camp and just the detail and the preparation that everybody puts in week to week. So, I feel really good about anybody that we will have out there that they will be ready to play."

Flowers has missed only three games to injury in his four seasons. The last time he was inactive was the 2024 AFC divisional playoff loss at Buffalo.

Baltimore has also ruled out Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike, who will have to wait another week to return from a significant neck injury. He had been limited in practice all week.

The Ravens also have three starters listed as questionable: linebacker Trey Hendrickson (finger), guard John Simpson (groin) and offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe).

Stanley has been sidelined for 45 games in his 10 seasons, but only one over the previous two. If he can't play, Carson Vinson would get his first career start.

"I think it is a really cool thing to see a guy really get in there and start to play, and his play style is exactly how we want to play," Minter said of Vinson. "He is very physical [and] he plays really aggressively, So, [I am] really happy with where he is at."

articles.headline: NFL Week 2 uniforms: Rams debut 'Classic Sol,' Ravens go all-white
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 2, led by a new alternate look from the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
Uniforms revealed in the offseason will make their respective debuts in Week 2. Fresh from their trip Down Under, the Los Angeles Rams look to win their first game of the season with a design rooted in its history.

Los Angeles will wear its "Classic Sol" alternate threads against the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football." The uniform honors the Rams' championship in 1951, with this season marking the 75th anniversary. A sol-colored jersey includes royal blue stitched and colored numbers. The three-stripe royal blue sleeve design is a direct nod to the uniforms worn in the 1951 season. The Giants will counter by going all-white.

The Baltimore Ravens underwent a closet redesign in the offseason, and with it came a new helmet and combination. Nicknamed "White Noise," Baltimore will pair all-white threads with the "Purple Rising" helmet against the New Orleans Saints. Baltimore originally revealed the purple lids in 2024, but tweaked them in April with a logo change, maintaining the metallic purple. It tops off a sleek new all-white look. 

It's an all-white look for the New York Jets as well, but from head-to-toe. New York unveiled new white helmets in July that differ from the throwback ones it typically wears with its classic uniforms. The Jets will pair it together with all-white jerseys and pants against the Green Bay Packers, who will wear their traditional home green on the road.

In the NFL "Rivalries" space, the Arizona Cardinals are the first to wear their design this season. Revealed last year, Arizona will rock it versus the Seattle Seahawks -- the same team they debuted it against in the previous campaign.

articles.headline: High-flying Brentford hammer struggling Chelsea
articles.description: Chelsea's winless run in the Premier League stretched to three matches as Brentford ran out deserved 3-0 winners at the Gtech Community Stadium.
articles.body:
Chelsea's winless run in the Premier League stretched to three matches as Brentford ran out deserved 3-0 winners at the Gtech Community Stadium.

It was a puzzling display for Xabi Alonso to ponder after watching his team impose themselves on the hosts in the first half yet struggling to find a goal threat, before succumbing in the second period to goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho.

This was a Chelsea lineup containing all the elements of their summer transfer rethink with a solid experienced spine which saw Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck make first Premier League starts.

Something appeared to have clicked. They did not look half as chaotic defensively in the first half as they have done at times this season, standing up physically to Brentford, winning duels and not allowing Keith Andrews' side to dominate second balls.

Yet old habits had followed the visitors on their short trip across west London. The marking from Mikkel Damsgaard's 61st-minute corner was poor, Jannik Schuster headed on and Anthony finished it off, then Thiago was left free to score after Kevin Schade's shot was saved.

It was then a low cross from the German that was whacked in during stoppage time by Carvalho to send Brentford fans into dreamland.

articles.headline: Olise nets hat trick, Kane makes history in Bayern rout
articles.description: Michael Olise scored his first Bayern Munich hat trick as the German champions romped to a 7-0 demolition of visiting Union Berlin in the Bundesliga on Friday.
articles.body:
Michael Olise scored his first Bayern Munich hat trick as the German champions romped to a 7-0 demolition of visiting Union Berlin in the Bundesliga on Friday.

Harry Kane also scored twice to become the fastest player to reach 100 goals in the Bundesliga

The 33-year-old England striker achieved the milestone by converting a 39th-minute penalty to extend Bayern's lead to 3-0 before halftime. Jamal Musiala had opened the scoring in the 18th, while Olise added another in the 43rd.

Kane struck again in the 54th, bringing his total to 101 goals in 99 matches. The previous record for the fastest to a century was set at 129 games by Dieter Müller, a prolific striker for Cologne in the 1970s.

Olise then completed a hat trick in the 73rd and 76th. The France forward's only previous career treble came earlier this year in an international friendly against Northern Ireland.  Ismael Saibari was also on target.

Following two unconvincing Bundesliga performances against promoted teams, a goalless draw with Schalke and a 2-1 win over Elversberg, the victory gave Bayern 10 points through four matches.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Nats reward ace Cade Cavalli with 4-year contract through 2030
articles.description: Pitcher Cade Cavalli and the Washington Nationals have agreed to a four-year contract through the 2030 season, a deal that includes a team option for 2031.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON -- Pitcher Cade Cavalli and the Washington Nationals agreed Friday to a four-year contract through the 2030 season, a deal that includes a team option for 2031.

Cavalli and the team agreed in January to a one-year contract guaranteeing $862,500: an $862,500 salary this year and a $4 million team option for 2027 with a $7,500 buyout. He would have been eligible for free agency after the 2029 season

"We've seen firsthand the work he's put in, the challenges he's overcome and the way he continues to grow as a pitcher, a person and a leader," president of baseball operations Paul Toboni said in a statement. "Our organization has tremendous belief in Cade, and, more importantly, we're incredibly proud to have him represent the Washington Nationals for years to come. We're so excited to watch the next chapter of his career unfold here with us."

Cavalli, who turned 28 on Aug. 14, is 12-5 with a 3.12 ERA this season and is tied for ninth in the major leagues with 194 strikeouts. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 29 of his 31 starts this season, the most in baseball.

Washington selected him with the 22nd pick in the 2020 amateur draft. He debuted in 2022, then was injured the following spring training and had Tommy John reconstructive elbow surgery that caused him to miss all of '23 and most of '24.

Cavalli made it back to the Nationals by August of last year and this season was their opening day starter.

"Since we drafted Cade in 2020, we've been continually impressed with who he is as a baseball player and as a human being," owner Mark Lerner said. "He's shown that he not only has the talent to excel as a major leaguer, but he also possesses the high character and leadership qualities that make him a beloved member of our clubhouse and in the community."

articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 2
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

Jump to a section:

Superflex rankings (with QBs)

Standard flex rankings (RBs, WRs, TEs only)

-->
These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Lions-Bills game.

Week 2 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Bijan Robinson, RB1 vs CAR

Similarly, ample volume so far, especially in the passing game. 
 2. Christian McCaffrey, RB2 vs MIA

Don't question his volume ... yet. The 49ers can afford to be cautious with him.
 3. Lamar Jackson, QB1 vs NO

For perspective, he hadn't thrown for 300 yards in a game in nearly two years. He's back!
 4. Caleb Williams, QB2 vs MIN

The bar is set high. Don't disappoint us, Caleb. We want 30 fantasy points every week now.

No, I am not worried about the Rams after one game in Australia. Not. At. All.

He ran against the Commanders, but we need to see it consistenly to really believe.
 7. Brock Purdy, QB4 vs MIA

Home game with Miami drives this optimistic ranking, but Purdy deserves it. 
 8. Dak Prescott, QB5 vs WSH

We expected more versus the Giants, but again, it was one game. He will be better.
 9. Jayden Daniels, QB6 @ DAL

Capable outing in the loss in Philadelphia, but not a dynamic one. 
 10. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR2 @ ARI

As this ranking shows, the change in Seattle's QB isn't destroying this star's value.
 11. Ja'Marr Chase, WR3 @ HOU

Yep. We may say it 50 times in this article. It was one game. Chase is still awesome.
 12. CeeDee Lamb, WR4 vs WSH

 13. Patrick Mahomes, QB7 vs IND

 14. Jaxson Dart, QB8 @ LAR

 15. Justin Herbert, QB9 vs LV

 16. Jonathan Taylor, RB3 @ KC

 17. Ashton Jeanty, RB4 @ LAC

He rushed for 100 yards only twice as a rookie. Let's hope Week 1 wasn't because he played Miami.
 18. Derrick Henry, RB5 vs NO

Hey, you passed him up on draft day because of his age. Does he look too old to you?
 19. Justin Jefferson, WR5 @ CHI

He has already matched last season's TD total. He needs only competent QB play. He has it now.
 20. Drake Maye, QB10 vs PIT

There aren't many easy ones on this season's schedule, but Maye should remain a QB1.

We all assumed fewer than 46 TD passes. He can still reach 30. Remain confident.
 22. Bo Nix, QB12 vs JAX

Christian Scott recorded his third quality start of the season last time out. With a 28.0% strikeout rate, it seems like he should have more over 22 starts, but a high 10.2% walk rate and an inordinate number of foul balls drive up his pitch count. Most of Scott's control issues came early in the season; over his last 11 starts, his walk rate is a more palatable 8.8%. The New York Mets host the Philadelphia Phillies. Robert Gasser is making a case to be in the Milwaukee Brewers' playoff rotation with a 2.33 ERA and 1.19 WHIP over his past four starts, fanning 20 in 19 1/3 innings. Next up is a road date with the Baltimore Orioles and a below-average lineup with a high 26.6% strikeout rate versus left-handers.

articles.headline: Sources: Jazz, Keyonte George agree to 5-year, $157.5M extension
articles.description: The Utah Jazz and guard Keyonte George have agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million contract extension, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
Guard Keyonte George has agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million contract extension with the Utah Jazz, sources told ESPN.

The deal does not include a team or player option, sources said. The terms were finalized Friday after months of negotiations between George's agent Jason Ranne of The Team and Jazz president of basketball operations Austin Ainge.

George's new deal will account for approximately 16 percent of Utah's salary cap.

George, 22, the 16th overall pick in the 2023 draft, cemented himself as an essential piece of the franchise's foundation with a breakout campaign last season. He averaged 23.6 points and 6.1 assists per game while shooting 45.6% from the floor and 37.1% from 3-point range -- all career bests.

The Jazz envision George and Darryn Peterson, the No. 2 pick in this year's draft, emerging as one of the league's most dynamic backcourt duos.

Utah, which endured a rebuilding process in recent years, hopes to make a major leap toward competitiveness this season after acquiring two-time All-Star power forward Jaren Jackson Jr. at the trade deadline.

articles.description: We're grading the biggest free agent signings and extensions, including Keyonte George's extension with the Jazz.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

 Sept. 18: George, Jazz agree to extension 

Keyonte George terms: Five years, $157.5 million

Grade: C+

George was one of the breakout players of the 2025-26 season, averaging 23.6 points and 6.1 assists per game while making 37% of his 3-pointers. He also boosted his efficiency from 7-8% below average in his first two seasons to 5% above average last year, which made him one of the top offensive guards in the sport.

On its own, that trajectory -- combined with George's age, as he'll turn 23 in November -- makes him more than worthy of this new rookie extension, which will pay him an average of $31.5 million per year. For context, this contract will pay nearly $100 million less over half a decade compared to the possible 25% max (which Victor Wembanyama, another member of the 2023 draft class, signed earlier this offseason).

But the complication with analyzing George's new deal is uncertainty about his ability on the other end. The Jazz have been worse with George on the floor versus when he's off in every season of his career to date. The defensive swing has been particularly problematic: Per Cleaning the Glass, Utah's defensive rating was 6.7 points worse with George last season and 8.7 points worse in 2024-25. Both marks ranked in the bottom 10% of players leaguewide.

Because of that track record, advanced stats that factor in on/off data are much lower in their assessment of George than his shiny box score stats would suggest. DARKO rates George as the third-least-valuable defender in the league, and both estimated plus-minus and xRAPM put him all the way in last place. Other players in his range include the likes of Cam Thomas and Trae Young, who have proved difficult to build around because of their limitations.

It's possible that this indictment of George is attributable to Utah's noncompetitive status during his time there; the Jazz haven't exactly been concerned about finishing 30th, 29th and 29th on defense over the last three years, as they've sought high draft picks instead of regular-season wins. Perhaps in a more competitive situation going forward, George will prove himself a mediocre or even normally below-average defender, rather than the truly terrible defender that his current met

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 18

Jazz, George agree on a five-year, rookie-scale extension

Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George have agreed on a five-year, $157.5 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Tim MacMahon. George was the No. 16 pick in the 2023 draft and has averaged 17.2 points and 5.3 assists per game in his three seasons with the Jazz.

Sept. 17

Bey, Pelicans agree to three-year extension

New Orleans Pelicans' Saddiq Bey agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Bey averaged a career-high 17.7 points per game last season after missing all of the 2024-25 season with a torn ACL.

Sept. 16

Kings remain interested in Duren

The Sacramento Kings continue to loom in the background of Jalen Duren's restricted free agency with the incumbent Detroit Pistons.

Kings general manager Scott Perry met with Duren for dinner in Miami in early July and has maintained a level of steady interest in the ultimate outcome of Duren's free agency, though a path to acquire Duren this summer remains blocked.

The Pistons declined any legitimate conversation about a Duren sign-and-trade to the Kings for starting center Domantas Sabonis and have maintained a strong stance about their intention to keep Duren.

As ESPN reported earlier this month, the Pistons have a five-year offer in the $35 million per year range on the table, but that hasn't been enough to entice the disgruntled Duren to sign.

His greatest piece of leverage is a risky one -- the $9.6 million qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next summer, when Sacramento will have flexibility for the first time in Perry's tenure as general manager. Zach LaVine's $48.9 million contract and De'Andre Hunter's $24.9 million contract both expire, allowing the Kings to generate a max offer for Duren, should he be available.

But that would only be the case if Duren is willing to take a massive one-year paycut and accept the risk of the qualifying offer. Until then, the Kings remain in the background as an interested long-term suitor helping Duren's leverage. -- Anthon

This is it! The final week of the 2026 fantasy baseball season has arrived. If you've made it this far, congratulations! The final seven days should be a wild race to the finish line, both in the real game and in our own leagues.

Week 25 is one of the more balanced weeks on the schedule, with one exception: The Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees begin their week-opening series with a Tuesday doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. One of those games makes up their May 23 postponement. The extra game gives both teams a seven-game final week.

All of the other 28 teams play exactly six games -- and 14 of those 28 split those six games evenly between home and the road. This is a "quality over quantity" week when it comes to matchups analysis. Additionally, most teams begin their weeks on Tuesday, as there are only three games scheduled for Monday.

Remember that MLB schedules all games on its final day, Sunday, Sept. 27, to start within a 15 minute window of one another (between 3:05 p.m. and 3:20 p.m. ET). This is by design to try and heighten the drama of real-life playoff races, but it also creates many mad, 3-4 hour dashes to the finish line in fantasy baseball leagues.
